page: OVHcloud c3-320-flex is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the KVM hypervisor. The hardware foundation features dedicated AMD EPYC processors delivering 160 physical cores and 160 vCPUs without multithreading at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 320.0 GB, maintaining a strict compute-oriented 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 20 Gbps. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional parallel processing capabilities due to the high dedicated physical core count. In stress-ng testing, multi-core CPU throughput reached 288,708.87, ranking in the top 10% tier, alongside top-tier multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 1,213.65 GB/sec. Memory subsystem benchmarks recorded strong throughput with 228.92 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 92.38 GB/sec write bandwidth, scaling to 9,189.99 GB/sec for small cached blocks. In-memory operations yielded top-tier performance with Redis recording 164.63 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 52.27 GB/sec.

Single-threaded execution shows moderate characteristics relative to the instance's high parallel capacity. Single-core stress-ng scores placed in the top 25%, while single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks performed within the median 50% tier. In machine learning inference evaluations using CPU execution, prompt processing achieved top-tier throughput of 4,166.24 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model and 209.48 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model, although sequential token generation throughput remains constrained.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on disk capacity versus pure compute scale: the bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD serves basic root filesystem needs but requires external network storage volumes for data-intensive pipelines. Cost efficiency is maximized in horizontally parallelized and CPU-bound environments. The instance is well suited for distributed compilation, high-concurrency batch processing, CPU-based machine learning prompt processing, in-memory caching clusters, and scientific computing workloads requiring dedicated AMD EPYC core density.
description: OVHcloud c3-320-flex is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance featuring 160 dedicated AMD EPYC physical cores clocked at 2.3 GHz and 320.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a 2 GB per core ratio. Utilizing KVM virtualization, the platform includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, 20 Gbps baseline networking, and operates without GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core computing metrics, demonstrated by high-tier stress-ng multi-threaded throughput, 1,213.65 GB/sec multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and 164.63 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput remains strong with 228.92 GB/sec uncached reads. Given the compact 50 GB storage disk relative to its massive compute allocation, the configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency when deployed for parallel computation, large-scale continuous integration, CPU-based prompt evaluation, and high-concurrency in-memory workloads rather than localized data warehousing.
